why:
All four lines are PASS. Each one names a concrete wrong build and explains how the line catches it:
- Line 1: a build that only edits the docs, or one that prints "HELLO, ADA!!!" or "HELLO ADA". Running `--shout Ada` catches both because the line gives the exact output.
- Line 2: a build that "upper-cases every greeting". `node bin/greet.js Ada` would then print the wrong text.
- Line 3: a build that documents the flag "only in README.md, or only in the usage string". Reading docs/index.md catches it.
- Line 4: a build that "tests only a shout() helper" and never runs the CLI. The line requires a test that runs the CLI.

Everything the output cites matches the repository. bin/greet.js does skip arguments that start with `--`. test/greet.test.js has a cli test that checks 'Hello, Ada!'. package.json runs `node --test`, which picks up *.test.js files. pages.yml and the stderr usage text 'usage: greet <name>' are both real. No FAIL entries exist, so the FAIL part of the criterion doesn't apply.
